correctness.rationale: At infinity the superelliptic pole-order test gives exactly four regular differentials dx/y, dx/y², x dx/y², x² dx/y². I independently expanded (x⁵+ax+b)² and (x⁵+ax+b)⁴ mod7 and reconstructed the coefficient extraction matrices H1=(2a) and H2=[[5ab²,0,1],[4b³,6a²,0],[a⁴,5ab,0]]. Their determinant is 2a²(a⁵-b⁴). On a≠0 H invertible gives ordinarity; on a=0,b≠0 the semilinear Cartier block has a nilpotent chain of length3 and rank2, giving stable rank0 and a-number2 (a-number is NOT the Cartier stable rank). An independently written finite-field quotient-ring enumerator reproduced #points (8,50,344,2094) over GF(7^j), j=1..4. Newton identities and functional equation yield 1-77T⁴+2401T⁸ and p-adic slope multiplicities 4 each at 1/4,3/4. The exceptional geometric scaling C_{0,b}≅C_{0,1} works because λ⁵=μ³=b over algebraic closure. The discriminant cusp is (t⁴,t⁵), bijective off t=0 with piecewise G_m inverse; it has q points over all GF(7^n), giving q-1 exceptional and (q-1)² ordinary marked pairs, not geometric isomorphism-class counts. Exact computations check finite data; universal parameter claims rest on algebra.

value.rationale: The natural two-parameter family exhibits a nonreduced Hasse divisor with a sharp rank dichotomy and an intermediate-slope exceptional Newton polygon. The complete geometric and marked-parameter stratification identifies a meaningful family boundary; it is more than a routine substitution into a genus formula. Even if the a-number portion is already known, the doubled divisor and NP/census are independently motivated facts, subject to stated priority risks.
residual_risks: Only normalized marked coefficient pairs, not isomorphism-class counts or arbitrary genus-four curves.
